newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM says confident of election victory.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM says confident of election victory.

text.p: Japan's Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto pledged after dissolving the Lower House of parliament on Friday that he would fight elections believing in the victory of his Liberal Democratic Party (LDP).
"I will strive to fight elections believing in the victory of the LDP," the prime minister told a group of legislators of his party, the biggest in the three-party coalition.
Hashimoto said he had done his best in the eight months since he took office to find a way to tackle the problems of bad loans held by mortgage firms and rebuild trust with the people of Okinawa.

"We will come under storms of major reforms, and politics, society and the administration need to survive. I have decided to dissolve (the Lower House) believing that now is the only time for the people to consider the nation's future and set the direction for it," Hashimoto said.

Earlier, Hashimoto's cabinet formally set October 20 as the date for general elections. The polls will be the first under a system designed to make campaigning less costly and reduce graft. In place of the old multi-seat system, 300 seats will be decided on a first-past-the-post basis, with the other 200 selected by proportional representation.
Hashimoto's LDP favoured going before voters as early as possible before April, when an unpopular sales tax will be raised to five percent from the current three percent.
Hashimoto is expected to pin his hopes for a second term in office on an improving economy and his handling of a bitter dispute with Okinawa over U.S. military bases there.

The opposition Shinshinto (New Frontier Party) plans to attack the government for imposing the sales tax rise and offer its own plan for a drastic overhaul of the tax system and to cut bureaucratic red tape.
